title: How East Bay Landlords Can Talk With Tenants About Safety Without Promising More Than the Law Requires

findings.quote: A report is notice under Civil Code §1941.3, and what you do after notice is what courts look at.
findings.root_cause: The Quick Answer extends a lock/window-security statute to every kind of security report. The body correctly narrows its Key Facts row, but the summary and shared script lose that boundary. Section 1941.3(b) concerns notice of a deficiency covered by subsection (a), not every light, stranger or theft report.
findings.fix: Quick Answer replacement: “A report of a deficiency covered by Civil Code §1941.3 can put the landlord on notice; the statute allows a reasonable time to correct it. Other security reports may raise duties under other law, so assess and document each one.” Replace the fourth paragraph of both Video Script blocks with: “Fourth, as a best practice, acknowledge security reports promptly, assess the urgency, arrange needed repairs and keep a record. A report about a required lock can give notice under California's lock statute; other reports may raise different duties.”
findings.future_prevention: Preserve statutory subject matter and distinguish company response policy from statutory deadlines in summaries and scripts.

findings.quote: Tenants can always call the police
findings.root_cause: The heading, Key Facts, FAQ 4 and shared script omit the statute's abuse/crime/emergency and necessary-assistance conditions. This turns a scoped statutory protection into an unconditional statement. Source: Civil Code §1946.8(b)–(d).
findings.fix: Heading: “Protected calls for police or emergency help.” Key Facts and FAQ 4 replacement: “Civil Code §1946.8 protects calls made by or on behalf of someone facing abuse, crime or an emergency when the caller believes help is necessary. A lease cannot restrict those calls, and a landlord cannot penalize a tenant or resident for them. Documentation is not required to establish that belief.” Shared script replacement: “Third, don't discourage calls for help. California Civil Code section 1946.8 protects calls about abuse, crime or an emergency when the caller believes help is needed. A lease can't restrict those calls, and a landlord can't penalize a tenant or resident for them.”
findings.future_prevention: Check every compressed legal restatement against the same statutory conditions, including companion takeaways.

findings.quote: A single incident is rarely foreseeable.
findings.root_cause: This unsupported frequency claim generalizes the heightened foreseeability analysis for hiring guards into all precautions. The package-theft row also says “Whatever you've promised in writing,” which omits duties independent of a contract. Ann M. balances foreseeability against the burden of the particular precaution; it does not establish a universal wait-for-repetition rule.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: “Do not wait for a second incident before assessing a known hazard. The duty depends on the foreseeable risk and the burden of the proposed precaution; hiring guards involves a higher foreseeability threshold than simpler measures.” Replace the package-theft ‘Usually your job’ cell with: “Honor written commitments and assess reasonable measures for known risks in common areas you control.”
findings.future_prevention: Keep guard-specific holdings separate from basic maintenance and warning duties; do not frame contracts as the sole source of duty.

findings.quote: What to leave out: crime statistics you've pulled together yourself, a description of the neighborhood, and any claim about how often something happens at the building.
findings.root_cause: Advice meant to prevent unsupported marketing claims can read as advice to withhold known incident history, undercutting the article's O’Hara discussion. The later absolute “No statute requires a general crime bulletin” is not established by a cited authority or bounded jurisdictional review.
findings.fix: Replace the quoted sentence with: “Leave out unsupported safety ratings, speculative crime statistics and promises about outcomes. This does not mean withholding known material safety information: seek legal guidance about warnings or disclosures when specific incidents or hazards are known.” Replace “No statute requires a general crime bulletin.” with: “Whether an incident calls for a warning depends on the facts and applicable duties; ask an attorney about a specific incident or known hazard.”
findings.future_prevention: Review advice about omissions against the article's disclosure duties; avoid universal negative legal claims without support.

findings.quote: Emeryville: press 5 for dispatch or a police report
findings.root_cause: The 510-596-3700 number is corroborated by the city's police page. The specific menu option could not be independently verified: the cited DA PDF and Community Outreach page were unavailable. This is a limited verification gap, not evidence the option is wrong.
findings.fix: Remove only the unverified parenthetical. Use: “Oakland 510-777-3333, Berkeley 510-981-5900, Emeryville 510-596-3700.” Alternatively retain the parenthetical after verifying the current official routing instruction.
findings.future_prevention: Store current phone-routing evidence separately from verified base numbers.

findings.quote: Prefer video? Watch the video version, with chapter timestamps and a full transcript.
findings.root_cause: The same draft says the video is in production; no playable video or chapter timestamps are present. Browser preview returned a site 404, so editor validity, actual layout and generated schema could not be verified. Metadata and balanced block comments do not prove those checks pass.
findings.fix: Until production is complete, replace the invitation with: “The companion video is in production.” For publication, replace the production placeholder with the actual playable embed, add real chapter times and a recording-checked transcript, and verify the authenticated preview, generated schema and destination links. No embed ID or transcript text can be supplied before the recording exists.
findings.future_prevention: Separate draft-content review from production-readiness sign-off; never infer missing generated schema from raw post content.

findings.root_cause: The required CORNERSTONE-STRUCTURE ‘Before You [Act]’ checklist is absent between the AEBP observation and FAQ. A prose conclusion and earlier tables do not meet the current explicit checklist requirement.
findings.fix:
Insert after Bottom Line, before FAQ:
## Before You Talk With Tenants About Safety
- Check that each listed security feature exists and works.
- Replace unsupported safety promises with factual descriptions.
- Give tenants current maintenance and police contact information.
- Log reports, assess urgency and document follow-up.
- Ask counsel about known hazards, incident warnings and protected lock-change requests.
findings.future_prevention: Run the cornerstone structural manifest before creating WordPress drafts.

The script is correctly labeled as a script while recording is pending.
